newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Philippine March inflation seen at 4.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Philippine March inflation seen at 4.6 pct.

text.p: Stable food prices and lower fuel prices are expected to keep year-on-year Philippine inflation in March about steady at 4.6 percent compared with 4.4 percent in February, a Reuters poll showed.

The average figure taken from a forecast by six banks and securities firms this week is far below the 11.8 percent registered in March last year when the country experienced a severe shortage of rice.
The March inflation figure is expected to be announced on Friday or Monday.
"There's not much inflationary expectation that would propel something more dramatic than was recorded in February," said Cecilia Tanchoco, an economist at the Bank of the Philippine Islands.
Tanchoco predicted the lowest March inflation figure of 4.3 percent among those surveyed.
On a month-on-month basis, inflation could rise at the same pace of 0.4 percentage points in March, economists said.
Central Bank officials have said they do not expect the March inflation figure to deviate much from February's 4.4 percent inflation rate.
"Basically, it's still your food numbers which are low," said Joey Cuyegkeng, research head of ING Barings Securities. Food prices comprise 58.47 percent of the consumer price index.
Another contributing factor was last month's price cuts in most petroleum products instituted by the country's three oil refiners due to lower crude prices in the world market, analysts said.
"It's the absence of price pressures during the month," added Lito Dalit, an analyst at AsianBank Corp.
He said domestic interest rates were lower in March, The bellwether 91-day Treasury bill rate averaged 10.063 percent in March against 10.658 percent in February.

It was also the first time since September 1995 that the rate on the T-bills had dropped to single-digit levels. On Monday, the 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to 9.498 percent from 9.724 percent the previous week. It has been at a single-digit level for three weeks.
The peso was slightly higher in March at an average of 26.337 to the U.S. dollar against an average of 26.341 in February as the currency was buoyed by proceeds of Europeso issuances.
Following are the inflation projections of analysts for March (in percentage terms):
All Asia Capital 4.9
AsianBank 4.5
Bank of the Phil Islands 4.3
ING Barings Securities 4.6-4.7
Peregrine Securities 4.5-5.0
SBC Warburg 4.6
Average 4.62
